16:1.sourceText: Κατήντησεν δὲ καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ εἰς Λύστραν. καὶ ἰδοὺ μαθητής τις ἦν ἐκεῖ ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος, υἱὸς γυναικὸς Ἰουδαίας πιστῆς πατρὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος,
16:1.targetText: And he came to Derbe and Lystra, and behold, a certain disciple was there, by name Timotheus, son of a certain woman, a believing Jewess, but of a father, a Greek,

groups.note: The two actual εἰς prepositions introduce the coordinated Derbe and Lystra destinations; English uses one shared to for that same pair.
The actual Ἰουδαίας is a feminine Jewish adjective, both tags A-GSF, rendered the personal designation a Jewess; the Greek adjective and genitive analysis remain.
The actual πιστῆς is the believing/faithful adjective, both tags A-GSF, rather than a source believing participle.

unmappedSource.reason: The additional καί before the first destination is not separately expressed as also; it is absent from the pinned TR wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR includes an additional τινος with woman, absent from N1904.

16:2.sourceText: ὃς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἀδελφῶν.
16:2.targetText: who was well testified to by the brothers in Lystra and Iconium;

groups.note: The actual μαρτυρέω attestation predicate is expanded was well testified to; there is no separately printed Greek well adverb.

16:3.sourceText: τοῦτον ἠθέλησεν ὁ Παῦλος σὺν αὐτῷ ἐξελθεῖν, καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς τόποις ἐκείνοις· ᾔδεισαν γὰρ ἅπαντες ὅτι Ἕλλην ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ὑπῆρχεν.
16:3.targetText: Paul wished this one to go forth with him, and having taken [him], he circumcised him, because of the Jews who are in those places, for they all knew his father—that he was a Greek.

groups.note: The actual αὐτόν is the same person taken and immediately circumcised; English repeats him with taking and circumcising, without an additional Greek object pronoun.

The actual nominative father is subject of the Greek was-a-Greek content clause. English first presents father as what was known and then resumes that same person as he; no additional source subject pronoun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Paul and the articles under those places/his father are not separately expressed.

16:4.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις, παρεδίδοσαν αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις.
16:4.targetText: And as they were going on through the cities, they were delivering to them the decrees to keep, that have been judged by the apostles and the elders who [are] in Jerusalem,

groups.note: The actual κεκριμένα is a perfect passive judging/deciding participle, rendered finite have been judged; its real participial form remains.

unmappedTarget.reason: The in-Jerusalem modifier has no written be verb; English supplies bracketed are. The article who does not carry a copula.

16:5.sourceText: Αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον τῷ ἀριθμῷ καθ’ ἡμέραν.
16:5.targetText: then, indeed, were the assemblies established in the faith, and were abounding in number every day;

groups.note: The actual καθ᾽ ἡμέραν is the distributive day expression; English every expresses κατά without a separately printed πᾶς adjective.

16:6.sourceText: Διῆλθον δὲ τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν, κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ·
16:6.targetText: and having gone through Phrygia and the region of Galatia, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia,

groups.note: The actual διῆλθον is a finite aorist active third-person plural going-through predicate. The pinned TR has the participle διελθόντες behind English having gone through; the actual N1904 finite form is retained.
The actual Γαλατικήν is the territorial Galatian adjective, rendered of Galatia with region; it is not an independently printed Greek Galatia place-name.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Phrygia and Asia are not separately expressed.

16:7.sourceText: ἐλθόντες δὲ κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν πορευθῆναι, καὶ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰησοῦ·
16:7.targetText: having gone toward Mysia, they were trying to go on toward Bithynia, and the Spirit did not permit them,

unmappedSource.reason: The narrative δέ connective is not separately expressed at this English verse opening.
The articles before Mysia and Bithynia are not separately expressed.
The actual genitive Jesus name qualifies Spirit in N1904; pinned TR and this English reading omit that name. No Jesus word is invented in the shorter English phrase.

16:8.sourceText: παρελθόντες δὲ τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα.
16:8.targetText: and having passed by Mysia, they came down to Troas.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Mysia is not separately expressed.

16:9.sourceText: καὶ ὅραμα διὰ νυκτὸς τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη, ἀνὴρ Μακεδών τις ἦν ἑστὼς καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν.
16:9.targetText: And a vision through the night appeared to Paul—a certain man of Macedonia was standing, calling on him, and saying, “Having passed through to Macedonia, help us.”

groups.note: The actual ὤφθη is an aorist passive of see, rendered appeared; it is not a different appearing verb.
The actual Μακεδών is the ethnic/personal designation Macedonian, both tags N-NSM; English of Macedonia does not imply a separately printed place-name at this position.
The actual ἑστώς is a perfect active standing participle with the written was verb; English standing does not change it into a source present participle.

unmappedSource.reason: The additional coordinator between standing and calling is not separately expressed in this English sentence.

16:10.sourceText: ὡς δὲ τὸ ὅραμα εἶδεν, εὐθέως ἐζητήσαμεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν, συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεὸς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς.
16:10.targetText: And when he saw the vision, immediately we endeavored to go forth to Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the LORD has called us to preach good news to them,

groups.note: The actual συμβιβάζω is one concluding/inferencing verb, rendered assuredly gathering; there is no separate Greek assuredly adverb or gathering verb printed here.
The actual αὐτούς is the accusative personal gospel-recipient complement, rendered to them; the source is not a Greek dative pronoun or independent to preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 names ὁ Θεός, God, whereas the pinned TR and English name the Lord; the different article/name expression remains a whole witness gap.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR Lord name instead of N1904 God; no Lord lemma is assigned to the actual Θεός token.

16:11.sourceText: Ἀναχθέντες δὲ ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην, τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς Νέαν Πόλιν,
16:11.targetText: having set sail, therefore, from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, on the next day also to Neapolis,

targetPhrases.text: we came with a straight course

groups.note: The actual εὐθυδρομέω is a single sail/run-straight verb, expanded we came with a straight course; there is no independent coming verb, straight adjective, or course noun here. Primary lexical entry: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/euthudromeo .
The actual dative article and coming/following participle designate the following day with the day noun understood, rendered on the next day.
The two actually written words Νέαν Πόλιν, new city, form the one English place-name Neapolis. Both actual adjective and city-noun identities remain linked to that name.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has δέ where the pinned TR reads οὖν, followed by English therefore; the different connectives remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows pinned TR οὖν at this point, rather than N1904 δέ.

16:12.sourceText: κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Φιλίππους, ἥτις ἐστὶν πρώτη τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας πόλις, κολωνία. Ἦμεν δὲ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει διατρίβοντες ἡμέρας τινάς.
16:12.targetText: there also to Philippi, which is a principal city of the part of Macedonia—a colony. And we were abiding in this city some days;

groups.note: The actual κἀκεῖθεν contracts and from there, rendered there also; the original from-there form is retained without inventing a separate also adverb.
The actual πρώτη is the first adjective, rendered principal in the city designation; it is not an independent Greek principal-city noun.

16:13.sourceText: τῇ τε ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ἐνομίζομεν προσευχὴν εἶναι, καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς συνελθούσαις γυναιξίν.
16:13.targetText: on the day of the Sabbaths we also went forth outside of the city, by a river, where there used to be prayer, and having sat down, we were speaking to the women who came together,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual genitive article/gate phrase names the gate; the pinned TR and English instead name the city. The different nominal heads remain a whole source/target witness gap.

The actual ἐνομίζομεν is first-person plural active we thought or supposed, both tags V-IAI-1P. The pinned TR instead has impersonal passive ἐνομίζετο, was customary; the different predicate framing is not conflated.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR city noun instead of N1904 gate; no city lemma is invented for the actual gate token.
The English habitual/impersonal framing follows TR ἐνομίζετο instead of N1904 first-person we supposed. The separate actual being infinitive remains linked to to be.

16:14.sourceText: καί τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία, πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων, σεβομένη τὸν Θεόν, ἤκουεν, ἧς ὁ Κύριος διήνοιξεν τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς λαλουμένοις ὑπὸ Παύλου.
16:14.targetText: and a certain woman, by name Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, worshiping God, was hearing, whose heart the LORD opened to attend to the things spoken by Paul;

groups.note: The actual πορφυρόπωλις is a single purple-seller compound person noun, expanded a seller of purple; no independent seller or purple noun is printed.
The actual dative article nominalizes the spoken content, rendered to the things; there is no independent Greek thing noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before God and the article under whose heart are not separately expressed.

16:15.sourceText: ὡς δὲ ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς, παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με πιστὴν τῷ Κυρίῳ εἶναι, εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου μένετε· καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς.
16:15.targetText: and when she was immersed, and her household, she called on us, saying, “If you have judged me to be faithful to the LORD, having entered into my house, remain”; and she constrained us.

groups.note: The one actual ἡμᾶς supplies the same visitors called on and then constrained in this immediate invitation. English repeats us with the first urging predicate; no additional Greek recipient pronoun is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles under her household and my house are not separately expressed.

16:16.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ πορευομένων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν, παιδίσκην τινὰ ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα Πύθωνα ὑπαντῆσαι ἡμῖν, ἥτις ἐργασίαν πολλὴν παρεῖχεν τοῖς κυρίοις αὐτῆς μαντευομένη.
16:16.targetText: And it came to pass in our going on to prayer, a certain maid, having a spirit of Python, met us, who brought much employment to her masters by soothsaying;

The actual genitive ἡμῶν is the personal subject of the going construction, expressed as possessive our in English.

The actual Πύθωνα is accusative, both tags N-ASM, as the Python designation with spirit; pinned TR has genitive πύθωνος. English of Python preserves the designation with the different case construction explicit.
The actual μαντευομένη is a divining present nonactive participle, rendered by soothsaying as the means of the work; no independent Greek by preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before prayer is not separately expressed in English.

16:17.sourceText: αὕτη κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι δοῦλοι τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου εἰσίν, οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας.
16:17.targetText: she having followed Paul and us, was crying, saying, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who declare to us [the] way of salvation!”

groups.note: The actual κατακολουθοῦσα is a present following participle, while pinned TR has an aorist participle; English having followed does not change the N1904 source form.

The actual ὑμῖν is second-person plural to you, while the pinned TR and English have first-person to us; the different addressed groups remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR first-person ἡμῖν rather than N1904 second-person ὑμῖν.
English supplies the bracketed article before way; no Greek definite article is printed with the actual ὁδόν noun.

16:18.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας. διαπονηθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς· καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ.
16:18.targetText: And this she was doing for many days, but Paul having been grieved, and having turned, said to the spirit, “I command you, in the Name of Jesus Christ, to come forth from her”; and it came forth the same hour.

groups.note: The actual αὐτῇ is the same intensifying demonstrative use with hour, rendered same with its separately written article; it is not a different personal recipient pronoun.

16:19.sourceText: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν, ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας,

unmappedSource.reason: The article under her masters and the articles before Paul and Silas are not separately expressed.

16:20.targetText: and having brought them to the magistrates, they said, “These men being Jews exceedingly trouble our city;

groups.note: The actual ἐκταράσσω is a single intensely-troubling verb, rendered exceedingly trouble; there is no independent Greek exceedingly adverb.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under These men and the article under our city are not separately expressed.

16:21.sourceText: καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν.
16:21.targetText: and they proclaim customs that are not lawful for us to receive nor to do, being Romans.”

groups.note: The actual ἔξεστιν is the impersonal is-permitted/lawful predicate, rendered are lawful with the English customs subject; it is not a Greek plural be verb plus adjective.

16:22.sourceText: καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν,
16:22.targetText: And the multitude rose up together against them, and the magistrates having torn their garments from them, were commanding to beat [them] with rods,

groups.note: The actual περιρήγνυμι is the stripping/tearing-off verb, rendered having torn in the clothing-removal expression; the source does not describe a separate generic garment-tearing verb. Primary entry at Acts16:22: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/periregnymi .

16:24.sourceText: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ ξύλον.

16:25.sourceText: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν Θεόν, ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι·

16:26.sourceText: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας, ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου· ἠνεῴχθησαν δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι, καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη.

16:34.targetText: having also brought them into his house, he set food before [them], and was glad with all the household, he having believed in God.

groups.note: The actual αὐτούς names the same pair brought into the house and given the meal in the immediate setting-before clause. English repeats them as the meal recipients; one actual accusative participant identity is retained, without an additional recipient pronoun.

The actual τράπεζα is the table noun used for the meal set before people, rendered food; it is not a Greek τροφή noun. Primary lexical entry and Acts16:34 example: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/trapeza .
The actual πανοικεί is one all-household adverb, expanded with all the household; there is no independent with preposition, all adjective, or household noun in that word.
The actual πεπιστευκώς is a singular nominative masculine perfect active participle, rendered he having believed; the real singular participial form remains.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under the English his house expression is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional αὐτοῦ house-possessor pronoun, absent from N1904; no independent house-owner pronoun is invented.

16:35.sourceText: Ἡμέρας δὲ γενομένης ἀπέστειλαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ τοὺς ῥαβδούχους λέγοντες Ἀπόλυσον τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐκείνους.
16:35.targetText: And day having come, the magistrates sent the rod-bearers, saying, “Let those men go”;

groups.note: The actual ῥαβδούχους is one rod-bearing official compound noun, rendered rod-bearers; rod and bearing are not separate Greek words.

unmappedSource.reason: The article under those men is not separately expressed.

16:36.sourceText: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ τοὺς λόγους τούτους πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον, ὅτι Ἀπέσταλκαν οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἵνα ἀπολυθῆτε. νῦν οὖν ἐξελθόντες πορεύεσθε ἐν εἰρήνῃ.
16:36.targetText: and the jailor told these words to Paul, “The magistrates have sent, that you may be let go; now, therefore, having gone forth go on in peace”;

unmappedSource.reason: The article under these words and the article before Paul are not separately expressed.
The quotation-introducing ὅτι is not separately expressed before the direct speech.

16:37.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους, ἀνθρώπους Ῥωμαίους ὑπάρχοντας, ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν· καὶ νῦν λάθρᾳ ἡμᾶς ἐκβάλλουσιν; οὐ γάρ, ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ἡμᾶς ἐξαγαγέτωσαν.
16:37.targetText: and Paul said to them, “Having beaten us publicly uncondemned—men, being Romans—they cast [us] to prison, and now privately they cast us forth! Why no! But having come themselves, let them bring us forth.”

groups.note: The actual first ἡμᾶς names the same people publicly beaten and immediately cast into prison. English repeats us for casting; the later private-casting and bringing-forth clauses have their own distinct written us tokens.
The actual οὐ γάρ negative-particle expression forms the emphatic rebuttal, rendered Why no; Why is not a separately printed Greek interrogative word.
The actual nominative αὐτοί intensifies the coming/bringing agents, rendered themselves; it is not an accusative reflexive object.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Paul is not separately expressed.

16:38.sourceText: ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ τοῖς στρατηγοῖς οἱ ῥαβδοῦχοι τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα. ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ῥωμαῖοί εἰσιν,
16:38.targetText: And the rod-bearers told these sayings to the magistrates, and they were afraid, having heard that they are Romans,

unmappedSource.reason: The article under these sayings is not separately expressed.

16:39.sourceText: καὶ ἐλθόντες παρεκάλεσαν αὐτούς, καὶ ἐξαγαγόντες ἠρώτων ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως.
16:39.targetText: and having come, they implored them, and having brought [them] forth, they were asking [them] to go forth from the city;

groups.note: The actual αὐτούς identifies the same immediate implored, brought-out, and requested-to-leave pair. English repeats them with bringing and asking; one original object identity remains, without two additional pronouns.

16:40.sourceText: ἐξελθόντες δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς φυλακῆς εἰσῆλθον πρὸς τὴν Λυδίαν, καὶ ἰδόντες παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐξῆλθαν.
16:40.targetText: and they, having gone forth out of the prison, entered into [the house of] Lydia, and having seen the brothers, they comforted them, and went forth.

groups.note: The actual πρός gives the visit destination Lydia, rendered into with the English supplied-house expression; the source preposition is not changed to εἰς.
The actual article/brothers is the same group seen and immediately comforted. English first names the brothers and resumes them as the comforted object, without an additional source pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Lydia is not separately expressed as a personal-name article in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the bracketed house location with Lydia; N1904 names Lydia directly after πρός and has no independent house noun here.
